title: Consumer Credit — G.19 (Aug 2026 data; revolving/BNPL financing of the August spend)
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/releases/g19/current/g19.pdf states its own rule verbatim — 'release is generally issued on the fifth business day of each month' and 'For release at 3 p.m. (Eastern Time)' (PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08). That rule reproduces the observed June-data date exactly (2026-08-07 was the fifth business day of August), and the fifth business day of October 2026 is Wednesday 2026-10-07 (Oct 1, 2, 5, 6, 7), covering August 2026. Filed estimate on three counts: the word is 'generally', the Board's own Statistical Release Schedule page could not be reached this session (federalreserve.gov/feeds/release_schedule.html returned 404, recorded in the proposing ledger's probe-ref.blocked), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is a derivation from a primary rule plus one verified instance, not a published calendar row. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: The financing side of a thesis the proposing ledger has carried without a measurement since 2026-09-01: August retail dollars are up while units are flat, and the record $43.3B K-12 back-to-school total (from $39.4B in 2025) was explicitly funded on BNPL and revolving credit against 'moderate at best' unit demand. G.19 is the hard-data Fed release that answers whether that gap was borrowed — and the 2026-10-07 edition is the one covering AUGUST, the same reference month as retail-sales-2026-09-16, landing 8 days before its successor print retail-sales-2026-10-15. That makes it the corroborating read on this doc's price-not-volume base case rather than a duplicate of it: Census measures the dollars, G.19 measures whether households funded them out of income or credit. Recent context from the June-data release (2026-08-07, primary): revolving credit +3.9% annualized in Q2 and +6.0% in June, against -4.7% in May and +10.5% in April — a series volatile enough month to month that a single print is a data point, not a trend. Filed low impact deliberately, following the umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-09-11 precedent in this same lane: the calendar's header comment carries a standing judgment that second-order consumer reads are omitted, and while G.19 is hard data rather than a survey, it is a 15:00 ET release with no house playbook keyed to it (symbols: [], macro-print), so it widens caution and never licenses an entry. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED alongside it, so their absence reads as a decision: the 2026-09-08 G.19 edition (July data, 15:00 ET today) — inside this print's corridor but dated the day of discovery, so it has no foresight value as a calendar entry and is instead named in the proposing ledger's own call sheet; and the NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, whose August edition is genuinely adjacent but whose publication date could not be pinned to a primary this session, and which is exactly the second-order survey class the table omits. Note 2026-10-07 already carries fomc-minutes-2026-10-07 at 14:00 ET, so this would land an hour behind it on a crowded afternoon. Discovered during the retail-sales-2026-09-16 D-8 pulse (2026-09-08).
